title: Batch Phalanx: continuous workload-profile-driven batching recommender and safe-apply playbook
creator: Jun Park
description:
Goal: build a continuous batching recommendation engine (codename: Batch Phalanx) that produces per-workload batching and KV-cache policy recommendations, validates them via a shadow/canary pipeline, and performs safe automatic apply and rollback when economic or quality regressions are detected.

Scope: workload profiling (request shape, seq lengths, latency sensitivity), heuristic rule engine to propose candidate microbatch sizes / max latency targets / prefix-caching policies, an experimental shadow-apply system for safety validation, and an operator-facing safe-apply playbook that supports gradual rollout, throttled apply windows, and automatic rollback triggers tied to SLOs and cost deltas.

Non-goals: model-level changes (quantization selection is out-of-scope for this ticket), user-facing UI polish (Console integration will be follow-up), and billing pipeline changes (cost signals will be read-only inputs).
comments: 2026-02-11 - Jun Park: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreed on three phases: (1) profiler, (2) heuristic recommender, (3) safe-apply pipeline. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Batch+Phalanx+Design

2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Prototype profiler emits workload signatures (median-seq, 95th-latency, burstiness score). Initial run over 7 days of traffic shows 18% token-cost saving potential in 12% of workloads. Queries and scripts in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-tooling/pull/214
2026-03-03 - SRE review (Marco Ruiz): telemetry ingestion nodes added; observed slight memory pressure during very large trace windows. Will add backpressure + retention cap before shadow apply.

2026-03-08 - QA (Elena Morales): Shadow canary test harness executed against dedicated test cluster. Two regressions detected under tail-latency microbursts; added guardrail to avoid microbatch increases when burstiness > 0.7.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Draft of safe-apply playbook pushed. Includes: preflight metrics, gradual window (5% -> 20% -> 100%), automatic rollback criteria (latency p99 increase > 15ms or quality-sanity failing > 2% or cost savings < 2% over 6 hours). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/322
steps: Implement workload profiler: sample across regions and model variants, compute signature vector (median_len, p95_latency, burstiness, prefix_reuse_ratio, KV_cache_hit_estimate)
Build heuristic engine: rules + tunable weightings that convert signature -> candidate params (microbatch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, enable_prefix_cache boolean, kv_cache_ttl_ms)
Deploy shadow-canary pipeline: apply candidate config in shadow mode for a configurable window; collect latency, error-rate, and synthetic quality checks
Create safe-apply controller: support % rollout steps, operator pause/resume, and automated rollback triggers based on thresholds
Integrate cost signal: compute expected per-token delta and require minimum cost benefit threshold before promoting changes
Telemetry & dashboards: per-workload dashboard for before/after, diff views, and alerting for rollback conditions
acceptance_criteria: Profiler runs on historical 14-day window and produces stable signature for >95% of active workloads
Heuristic engine recommends candidate configs that on shadow runs show no p99 latency regression > 10ms for 95% of test cases
Safe-apply supports staged rollout with automatic rollback when thresholds exceeded
Operator runbook documented and validated in tabletop exercise
End-to-end test demonstrating at least one safe apply that yields >5% cost-per-token improvement without violating latency SLOs
notes: Design decision: start with rules + supervised weighting rather than full RL to keep rollout explainable to SRE and customers
Trade-off: more aggressive batching yields cost wins but increases sensitivity to bursts; introduced burstiness score and conservative caps to mitigate
Open question: whether to expose suggested 'expected cost delta' to customers in Console. Tentatively planned for runtime-2.5
Follow-ups: Console UI card for 'Batching Recommendations', and API hook to accept/decline automated applies (PM-owned)
